title: Install a clip-on CPU cooler without lifting it off its pre-applied paste
instruction: Install the CPU cooler on the processor. Lower it straight onto the processor and, once its thermal paste touches, don't lift it off again or slide it more than 10 mm. Then press each end of its clip down until it hooks over the lug, and push the lever over and down until it locks.
context: AMD's boxed coolers ship with thermal material pre-applied, and AMD's installation guide for its boxed processors says: 'If you remove the heatsink/fan after initial installation, you must first clean the heatsink surface and apply new thermal interface material before reinstalling the heatsink/fan on your processor.' Its builder's guide adds: 'Do not use the thermal interface material if it has scratches or gaps' and 'The heatsink must have full contact with the processor.' So the cooler has to go down right the first time: set down off-centre and lifted to try again, or dragged across the processor, it leaves gaps, and the processor runs hot and throttles. The finished install looks the same either way, so the rule is scored over the whole trial. Unlike the accepted processor install (the socket's own lever), this is the cooler on top, with a stated rule the robot must keep while it works.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights are above the table top. Motherboard: an ATX board (305 x 244 mm, 1.6 mm black PCB with memory slots, VRM heatsinks, M.2 heatsinks and an x16 slot), lying flat on the table and fixed to it, its long side along y, centred at (0.282, -0.064). Its CPU socket is at (0.290, 0.000) with an AMD-style processor in it (40 x 40 mm lid, its top 9.7 mm above the table). Around the socket a black plastic retention frame 62 x 98 mm (x by y) has a lug on each end face, at y = +0.049 and -0.049: 6 mm wide (x), sticking out 4 mm (along y), its flat underside 5.0 mm above the table and its top sloping from 9.0 mm at the frame down to 6.5 mm at its tip. Cooler, after AMD's boxed AM2/AM3 coolers and their clip mount (0.36 kg, 88 x 84 x 65 mm without the clip): a 40 x 40 mm copper base 1.5 mm thick with a 30 mm square of grey thermal paste pre-applied under it (as boxed coolers ship), an 88 x 84 x 38.5 mm aluminium fin block with two 6 mm copper heat pipes up its sides, and a 76 x 76 x 22 mm black plastic fan cover on top with a 66 mm fan. A steel clip runs across its middle along y; each end bends down into a leg (18 mm wide, 1.2 mm thick) 50.5 mm from the cooler's centre, with a 12 x 5.3 mm window near its bottom, and at its top a press tab reaching 9 mm out. Each leg is sprung up and can flex outward. On the right end a black lever (32 x 8 x 4 mm, grooved grip) turns on a pin 21 mm beyond the leg, 38 mm above the cooler's base, in the plane of the leg; it leans 25 degrees towards +x, unlocked. The cooler stands on a 40 x 40 x 15 mm dark grey foam block at (0.290, 0.200), the clip along y with the lever on the right, legs hanging free beside the block.
scoring: Tools: the trial video, a ruler, top and side photos, and the paste print on the processor (seen when the cooler is lifted off for the reset). Paste rule, for the whole trial: once the base first touches the processor, it never lifts more than 3 mm off it, and its centre never moves more than 10 mm sideways from where it first touched. Setting it back down in place afterwards does not undo a lift. On real arms this is read from the video and the print (one square, not doubled or torn into ridges, not wiped more than 10 mm); in simulation it is checked on every control step from the cooler's pose. Seated: the cooler's base on the processor, its centre within 3 mm of the processor's, square with the socket within 5 degrees (the clip along y), tilted less than 3 degrees, base within 1.5 mm of the processor's top. Released: no part of the robot touches the cooler. A clip end is hooked when its lug shows through the leg's window and the leg hangs straight (within 1.5 degrees), pulled up against the lug's underside. Locked: the lever has gone over the top and lies flat along -x. 0 if the paste rule is broken, or the cooler is not seated or not released. 0.25: seated and released. 0.5: and one clip end hooked. 0.75: and both clip ends hooked. 1.0 (success, held for 1 s): and the lever locked. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Push the lever back up to lean 25 degrees towards +x, press each clip end's tab down and pull its leg out off its lug, lift the cooler off and stand it on the foam block, clip along y, lever on the right. Wipe the paste off the processor and the base and apply a fresh 30 mm square (a stencil and about 0.3 g of paste) before each trial.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control; board fixed. Each clip leg slides on a spring (600 N/m) and flexes outward on another; pressing a tab down rides it over its lug (about 6 mm). The lever's over-centre spring and cam pull the clip tighter as it locks. The clip's bending, fins and fan are simplified; no thermal contact is simulated; the paste is not simulated, its rule is checked from the base's pose against the processor every step.
